messages.subject: Proof review succeeded with explicit restrictions
messages.body: I independently checked the harmonic, probability/logit-transfer and weighted-KL proofs and verified core.py and student.py against the requested d5a45f3 Git blobs without changing files. The statements hold with the proof repairs detailed in the attached review payload: zero-margin ties, export-set teacher errors, global permission and batch gating, and the valid-checkpoint scope of all-UNKNOWN invariance. This proof-review task is complete; empirical semantic goodness, head mismatch, target-population KL and clinical performance remain unverified and outside scope.

{"taskId":"task_9a0ff574e706","dispatchId":"ctx_12adf3cffd77","outcome":"succeeded","review":"INDEPENDENT SKEPTICAL PROOF REVIEW — 2026-10-13
Scope: read-only mathematical/source review of immutable /tmp/self-audit-scientific-20261012-d5a45f3, requested commit d5a45f31481f0a702a1f9d5d418889fe704e9105. No source/config/report files edited; no training, data evaluation, GPU, commits, or pushes. No broad survey. Pure scalar arithmetic checked with Python; proofs below are analytic, not empirical validation. I initially inspected ForFed Git metadata only before the coordinator redirect, and did not inspect its source files.

PROVENANCE
The snapshot core.py and student.py exactly match Git blobs at the requested SHA, independently verified with git rev-parse SHA:path and git hash-object:
src/self_audit_guidance/core.py = 7b2bb364ab35ff9013d0fe406c4ee55d8e2b3383
src/self_audit_guidance/student.py = 26925f20c1b15dd2b03825b3b4729007265baac1
This verifies the two audited files against the fixed commit, not a claim that today's moving remote main remains at that commit.

1. HARMONIC COMPARATOR: VALID WITH EXPLICIT DOMAIN AND SEMANTIC ASSUMPTIONS
Let a finite state space be partitioned into S and U; P must be entrywise nonnegative and row stochastic. Every u in U must have a positive-probability path to S. Boundary values are clamped, Q_S=R_S, and Q_U=P_UU Q_U+P_US R_S. The original P need not make S absorbing: these statements concern the process killed on FIRST hitting S. Boundary outgoing transitions are irrelevant.

Proof of existence, stochasticity, and hitting interpretation:
Choose for each u a finite positive-probability path to S. Finiteness supplies a common length bound N and positive epsilon such that from every u the chance of reaching S within N steps is at least epsilon. With T=P_UU, row sums of T^(kN) are therefore at most (1-epsilon)^k. Hence spectral radius(T)<1 and (I-T)^(-1)=sum_{n>=0} T^n exists and is entrywise nonnegative. Let H=(I-T)^(-1)P_US. Since (I-T)1_U=P_US 1_S, H1_S=1_U. Also (T^n P_US)_{is} is the probability of surviving n steps in U and then first entering S at s, so H_is=Pr_i[X_tau=s] for tau=inf{t>=0:X_t in S}. Thus H is a row-stochastic absorption matrix and Q_U=H R_S is the unique Dirichlet solution.

Assume 0<=s_s<=1, V_s in the four-class simplex, u=(1/4,...,1/4), and R_s=(1-s_s)u+s_s V_s. Then
Q_i=(1-h_i)u+sum_s H_is s_s V_s, h_i=sum_s H_is s_s in [0,1].
For h_i>0, partition S into query-specific G_i and B_i, with V_{s,y_i}>=1-eta for all s in G_i and eta in [0,1]. Let b_i=sum_{s in B_i}H_is s_s/h_i. Nonnegativity of all bad-anchor coordinates gives
Q_{i,y_i} >= (1-h_i)/4 + (1-eta)sum_{s in G_i}H_is s_s
= L_i=(1-h_i)/4+h_i(1-b_i)(1-eta).
Bad must include both wrongly named anchors and semantically correct anchors from a DIFFERENT class than y_i, unless their target-coordinate bound is otherwise demonstrated. Badness and b_i are query-specific, not a universal label-corruption fraction. This is a deterministic weighted-mixture inequality: no independent anchors, witnesses, or samples are required. Its named-semantic premise is an assumption about true y_i, not an observable certificate obtained from the graph alone.

Entropy and acceptance proof:
Define Hmax(t)=-t log(t)-(1-t)log((1-t)/3), with 0 log 0=0. For a simplex Q with Q_y=t, concavity makes entropy maximal when the other three entries each equal (1-t)/3. Since Hmax'(t)=log((1-t)/(3t))<=0 for t>=1/4, Q_y>=L>1/2 implies entropy(Q)<=Hmax(L). It also implies unique argmax(Q)=y, max(Q)>=L, and top gap>=Q_y-(1-Q_y)>=2L-1. Therefore the exact comparator's three numeric gates pass correctly if L>1/2, L>=pmin, 2L-1>=mmin, and h[1-Hmax(L)/log 4]>=rmin, when reliability is EXACTLY h[1-entropy(Q)/log 4]. Any additional permission/status veto must also allow y; the theorem otherwise guarantees the numeric gates, not that an arbitrary export system emits a label. For approximate solves these are exact-solution statements: require certified error and threshold slack (for coordinate error e, use L-e and 2(L-e)-1, plus an appropriate reliability error bound). Do not silently use an approximate solver's values as exact.

Constructive graph:
For any finite n>=1, use hub v0, path v0-v1-...-vn with any positive finite conductances, and three boundary leaves s1,s2,s3 joined only to v0 with conductances 0.8,0.1,0.1. Each vertex has self-loop conductance 1, and P is the row-normalized conductance matrix. For any boundary harmonic coordinate f, the degree-one terminal equation implies f(vn)=f(vn-1); backward induction gives f(vk)=f(v0) along the whole path. The hub equation cancels its self-loop and path edge, leaving f(v0)=0.8 f(s1)+0.1 f(s2)+0.1 f(s3). Thus every U node has H_i=(0.8,0.1,0.1), regardless of n or positive path conductances. This also proves the hitting probabilities directly. Self-loops delay absorption but do not alter these probabilities.

Take true class LV at every U node and at s1,s2; true class RV at s3. At s1 let V_LV=0.98 and put the remaining 0.02 on RV for a fully specified example; at s2 (corrupted LV) and s3 (correct RV but cross-class influence) take V_RV=1. All strengths equal 0.98. Then h=0.98, b=0.2, eta=0.02, and L=0.005+0.98*0.8*0.98=0.77332. In BG,RV,MYO,LV order, Q=(0.005,0.21668,0.005,0.77332), true margin=0.55664, conservative margin bound=0.54664, Hmax(L)=0.784266956878085, reliability lower bound=0.425585555783665, and actual example reliability=0.5677588135125595. Hence numeric thresholds 0.70/0.20/0.05 pass correctly. The same correct conclusion holds for any allocation of the good leaf's remaining 0.02 using the lower bound. Distance from vn to the nearest boundary is n+1, so this is a family with arbitrarily distant correct accepted U nodes; it is not an infinite-graph claim or a uniform iteration/runtime bound.

Required edge cases and counterexamples:
- h=0 implies Q=u and reliability=0; b is undefined and must not be divided by zero. State this case separately, or set b=0 by convention only after establishing Q=u. No unique correct argmax follows; positive margin/reliability gates reject. Zero thresholds plus arbitrary tie-breaking could emit a label, so unconditional abstention must not be claimed without gates.
- If some U cannot reach S, a closed U class exists, I-P_UU can be singular, and boundary data do not determine that class. A disconnected unanchored component with self-loops is an immediate counterexample. Restrict to a closed set of states guaranteed to hit S, or explicitly abstain on unsupported components; mere existence of a path from one starting node is insufficient if it can also enter a trap.
- Perfect semantic anchors can still be too weak: with all strengths 0.2 and pure LV anchors, Q_LV=0.4 and reliability=0.007807190511263751, failing the stated defaults. In general max(Q)<=1/4+3h/4, so pmax>=0.70 requires h>=0.6, and guaranteed strict majority is impossible unless h>1/3. These are necessary strength conditions, not sufficient semantic conditions.
- Incorrect semantics can produce confident acceptance: all true LV but all V pure RV with strength 0.98 gives Q=(0.005,0.985,0.005,0.005), gap=0.98 and reliability=0.9132937776710048. All default numeric gates pass incorrectly. This does not refute the theorem, because its goodness/bound assumption fails.
- The example has two bad leaves out of three but bad INFLUENCE 0.2, showing why raw anchor counts cannot replace H-weighted strengths.

Repository boundary:
This is a classical Dirichlet/hitting comparator, not the implemented operator or a novelty result. core.py:147-168 instead solves Q=alpha R0+(1-alpha)P Q on ALL nodes, with alpha>0 (default 0.35 at line 31); make_bank lines 274-285 also propagates strengths with that same restart operator. Its kernel is K=alpha[I-(1-alpha)P]^(-1), not H, and boundary rows are not clamped. Setting alpha=0 is rejected and would not implement this Dirichlet problem. No conclusion here removes the current neutral-node hard-bank obstruction or establishes MRI semantic goodness.

2. PROBABILITY, LOGIT, AND RISK TRANSFER: VALID AFTER TIE AND SCOPE FIXES
Let p,q be distributions in a common four-class order, delta>=0, and ||p-q||_infinity<=delta at each point in scope. Define q's chosen hard label c, its top value qmax, and top gap gq=q_c-max_{k!=c}q_k. Export has pmax>=tau, top gap>=m, and a permitted argmax, with any additional status gate open.

Necessity:
If the student exports j, then qmax>=q_j>=p_j-delta>=tau-delta. This is necessary only, not sufficient; probability says nothing about permissions, gap, or truth.

Sufficiency:
If q's top c is permitted, q_c>=tau+delta, and gq>=m+2delta, then p_c>=tau and p_c-p_k>=q_c-q_k-2delta>=m for all k!=c. If m>0 this makes c uniquely top and the student emits c (provided its status gate is open). For arbitrary m=0 the non-strict statement is false without a tie rule guaranteeing c; repair it by requiring gq>2delta as well, or specifying a compatible tie rule. Concrete four-class counterexample: q=(0.4,0.6,0,0), p=(0.5,0.5,0,0), delta=0.1, tau=0.5, m=0, and only class 1 permitted. All proposed non-strict premises hold for c=1, but first-index argmax chooses disallowed class 0 and export abstains. Current GuidanceConfig enforces positive m, so the tie defect concerns the general proposition, not the current default configuration.

Argmax preservation:
gq>2delta implies p_c>p_k for all k!=c. At equality ties are possible as above, so the strict inequality is necessary for a tie-independent guarantee. This preserves a confidently WRONG teacher just as faithfully as a correct teacher; it establishes agreement, not semantics.

Softmax coordinate bound:
Let z,z' be logits at the same temperature 1 with ||z-z'||_infinity<=B. For sigma_j, its gradient has l1 norm sigma_j(1-sigma_j)+sum_{k!=j}sigma_j sigma_k=2 sigma_j(1-sigma_j)<=1/2. Integrating the directional derivative on the line segment between z and z' gives |sigma_j(z)-sigma_j(z')|<=B/2 for each j, hence ||p-q||_infinity<=B/2 (also cap at 1 if useful). At temperature T>0 the constant is 1/(2T). The local 1/2 constant is sharp in the balanced binary limit; do not confuse this infinity-to-infinity bound with a different norm or temperature.

Feature/readout bridge:
A precise sufficient bridge is q=softmax(g(f_t)), p=softmax(g_s(f_s)), ||f_s-f_t||<=e, ||g(a)-g(b)||_infinity<=L||a-b|| on the relevant domain, and ||g_s(f_s)-g(f_s)||_infinity<=kappa. Triangle inequality gives logit error B<=Le+kappa, then probability error <=(Le+kappa)/2. Both readout compatibility and the feature norm/pointwise scope must be specified. A feature match by itself supplies no kappa. In the actual model, student.py:23-32 emits project(high) for feature matching while semantic logits come from head(decode([low,interpolate(high)])); lines 34-35 identify decode/head as separate semantic parameters. Swapping semantic head output rows leaves project features unchanged while permuting named labels. Thus even exact feature matching can coexist with arbitrary named prediction error. Moreover, the actual feature objective is mean cosine loss on nonzero teacher vectors (lines 47-52); positive rescaling preserves perfect cosine while Euclidean error can grow without bound. A pointwise Euclidean e or compatible readout cannot be inferred from that loss. If BOTH compared features are normalized, squared pointwise distance equals 2(1-cosine), but an averaged loss is still not a uniform guarantee.

Conditional risk:
Let nu be the measure of interest, y truth, A the ACTUAL student export set with nu(A)>0, c_q=argmax(q) under a fixed tie rule, and F={gq<=2delta}. If the uniform probability error holds on A, then pointwise
1_A 1{argmax(p)!=y} <= 1_A 1{c_q!=y} + 1_{A intersect F}.
Indeed, outside F the argmax proof identifies the two predictions. Integrating and dividing gives
R_student(A) <= [nu(A intersect {c_q!=y})+nu(A intersect F)]/nu(A),
optionally capped at 1. This is error among accepted STUDENT outputs, not global risk or risk on a different teacher-accepted set. Teacher error must be defined using argmax(q) on ALL of A; counting errors only where the bank emitted a non-UNKNOWN hard label omits exactly the new-support cases. If the delta bound fails on some points, add the mass of that failure event. If nu(A)=0 this conditional risk is undefined, not zero accuracy error. No independence is required, and a tiny denominator or large teacher-error term can make the bound vacuous.

3. ADDED WEIGHTED-KL CLAIM: VALID, WITH A NECESSARY LOW-WEIGHT EXCEPTION
Let D=integral w KL(q||p) dnu, using natural logarithms, measurable nonnegative w and probability vectors, w0>0 and delta>0. Zero probabilities use the standard extended KL conventions. Put E_delta={||q-p||_infinity>delta}.
For every coordinate c, the log-sum inequality aggregates the other coordinates to give KL(q||p)>=kl(q_c||p_c). As a function of its first argument x at fixed v=p_c, binary KL has second derivative 1/[x(1-x)]>=4 and value/first derivative zero at x=v, hence kl(x||v)>=2(x-v)^2, extended to endpoints by limits. Choosing a coordinate attaining the finite-dimensional maximum gives KL(q||p)>=2||q-p||_infinity^2. No union bound and NO factor of four are needed.
On {w>=w0} intersect E_delta, the integrand exceeds 2w0 delta^2, so
nu({w>=w0} intersect E_delta) <= D/(2w0 delta^2).
For student export A with nu(A)>0, outside F={gq<=2delta}, {w<w0}, and E_delta, the teacher and student hard labels coincide. Therefore
R_student(A) <= [nu(A intersect {argmax(q)!=y}) + nu(A intersect F) + nu(A intersect {w<w0}) + D/(2w0 delta^2)] / nu(A).
Again cap at 1 if desired. This proves the coordinator's added statement; weights may depend arbitrarily on x, q, or the model, without any independence assumption.

The low-weight term cannot be deleted: take A to have unit measure, true class 0, q=(0.97,0.01,0.01,0.01), p=(0.01,0.97,0.01,0.01), both classes permitted and status open, delta=0.1, and w=0 everywhere. The teacher is correct, its gap is 0.96, the student confidently exports wrong class 1, and D=0. Without the low-weight term the claimed risk bound would be zero although actual risk is one; with it the bound is valid and vacuous. Replacing w=0 by a tiny positive epsilon also makes D arbitrarily small while error remains one unless w0/low-weight control is retained.
This is a same-measure bound. A finite or small empirical TRAIN objective does not establish D on unseen patients. Actual guidance_loss uses normalized batch soft CE, whose numerator equals weighted teacher entropy plus weighted KL, and also uses a batch activation gate; it is not a demonstrated population KL guarantee. Export has probability, margin, permission and checkpoint-status gates, but NO bank reliability gate (student.py:139-150), so low-weight mass on exported pixels can be large.

4. SOURCE AUDIT: EXACT SUPPORT AND INVARIANT QUALIFICATIONS
core.py:274-289 saves soft q and reliability independently of labels. Hard valid is the conjunction of probability, margin and reliability (line 285); labels are argmax or UNKNOWN=255 (286); hard class counts are taken from those labels (287).
student.py:77-80 builds class_patients from those HARD class_pixels and permits a class only if it has at least one hard-accepted pixel in at least two TRAIN patients. Therefore hard-bank acceptance DOES affect a global training permission. The correct distinction is that the per-pixel hard-accept mask is not the per-pixel soft training weight; do not claim hard acceptance is wholly irrelevant to training support.

Precisely, for pixel i in batch B:
a_c=1{hard accepted class c occurs in >=2 training patients};
w_i=rho_i a_argmax(q_i) (student.py:95-98);
enabled=any(a_1,a_2,a_3);
active_B=enabled AND exists j in B with argmax(q_j)!=BG and w_j>0 (lines 54-58).
If active_B, semantic CE is sum_i w_i[-sum_c q_ic log p_ic]/max(sum_i w_i,1e-8), over ALL four channels and all positive-weight pixels in that batch, including BG pixels. Otherwise the semantic term is zero. Thus a below-hard-threshold pixel can contribute if its top class is globally permitted and its batch is active; conversely positive w alone is insufficient in a BG-only batch. The target vector is NOT masked or renormalized to permitted channels. Its logit derivative, when active, is w_i(p_ic-q_ic)/denominator for every c, so even a disallowed non-argmax channel can receive semantic gradient. Export separately vetoes a disallowed argmax (147-150).

All-foreground-permissions-false invariant:
For checkpoints PRODUCED BY train_student with any(a_1,a_2,a_3)=false, semantic_enabled=false, every batch active=false, and successful_semantic stays zero. After loss.backward(), decode/head grads are explicitly set to None (101-105; semantic_parameters is 34-35), avoiding their optimizer/weight-decay updates. The feature objective still has its encoder/project path (47-52), so those parameters remain eligible to learn, subject to actual nonzero gradients and valid feature signal. There is no theorem that they change every step or acquire useful anatomy; all-zero teacher features raise NO_FEATURE_SIGNAL (50-51).
The resulting checkpoint status is REPRESENTATION_ONLY (116-120). predict_cine creates an all-255 output and immediately returns it for this status (141-142), so exported UNKNOWN is invariant under encoder feature learning in this training path. The semantic head weights can remain fixed while raw logits change with shared encoder features, but the export stays UNKNOWN.
Do NOT generalize the invariant to an arbitrary manually constructed inconsistent checkpoint: all FG permissions false, BG permission true, and a non-REPRESENTATION_ONLY status can still permit BG export. The proved invariant is the valid train_student -> checkpoint -> predict_cine path, and fixed permissions/status. Hard support/permission changes require a changed bank/retraining state, not an implication of feature loss reduction.

VERDICT
The harmonic construction, concentration/margin/entropy lower bound, softmax B/2 bound, conditional transfer inequality, and added weighted-KL inequality are analytically verified under the explicitly stated assumptions. Required repairs are the m=0 tie condition, teacher-error accounting across the full student export set, distinction between per-pixel soft support and global permissions/batch gates, and restriction of all-UNKNOWN invariance to checkpoints produced by the audited training path. None supplies admissible named-anatomical truth, a measured kappa or population D, new-patient accuracy/coverage, a deployed harmonic solver, or novelty evidence. No implementation or empirical work remains within this dispatched proof-review task."}
